This gives lambda_n=f(rho_n)(1+O(n^-1/2)) and (n+1)^(beta/2)lambda_n=b(rho_n)^(beta/2)+O(n^-1/2), b=Phi’/r. Adjacent saddles have gaps O(1/rho_n) while |b’|<=2M/r, hence the full b-tail interval is sampled. Spectral counting inversion for a positive decreasing sequence and convex forward/backward secant bounds establish the three iff conditions including disk averaged Laplacian identity 2Phi’(R)/R. Direct Gamma(n+1,1) moment computation for quadratic Phi=r²/2 at beta=1,2,4, n=50/200/800 confirms convergence of scaled ratios, not the uniform theorem. Oscillatory-Hessian and oscillatory-slope examples satisfy stated Hessian bounds.
